races.title: State Assembly, District 70
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Tri Ta
cands.bio: Born in Saigon, Vietnam; Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 70 since December 2022. Previously Westminster city councilmember from 2006, mayor pro tem from 2008, mayor from 2012 to 2022, and Orange County Water District director from 2018 to 2022.

controversies.text: In September 2019, while facing a recall effort, Mayor Ta proposed a Westminster resolution alleging the Vietnamese government was fueling turmoil at City Hall. Voice of OC reported he gave no specific evidence. The council passed it, with Ta, Ho and Nguyen in favor. Critics said it could label opponents communists. Ta didn't respond to reporters.

In January 2022 the Westminster council voted 3-2 to censure Mayor Ta over comments in Vietnamese-language media that a councilmember called false and defamatory. Ta called the allegations "completely irrational" and said he meant it was unclear where his new office would be. The censure is symbolic and has no legal force.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in 2026 by the Republican Party of California and Reform California, and recommended by several voter-guide groups listed on Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find documented actions or stated positions from Tri Ta on data centers, homestead property tax, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, donor money pledges, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year. His bill list was not readable in the pages we had, so we could not tie his bills to these topics. The pages do not say which year he first arrived in California, or whether he was raised anywhere other than Vietnam. No outside news reporting was available to confirm the censure or the recall details.

local.label: Roots 55: He came to the U.S. as a refugee at 19 in 1992, studied at Cal State LA, was elected to the Westminster, California city council in 2006, and lives in Westminster, which puts his adult life in California at roughly 20 or more years.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2022. Before that he was Westminster city councilmember (elected 2006), mayor pro tem (2008), mayor (2012–2022) and Orange County Water District director (2018–2022). He has authored bills on health coverage, utility rates and criminal law.
qual.why: Prior legislative service plus a long record in local elected office, including a mayoralty and a water district seat, puts him in the high range. Committee assignments were not counted, and no law or budget career outside elected office was found.

cands.name: Paula Swift
cands.bio: Dr. Paula Swift is a Democratic candidate for California State Assembly District 70. She is a small business owner and educator who runs a consulting firm and works as an adjunct professor. She holds a bachelor's from Azusa Pacific University and a master's and Ed.D. from USC. She has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, California Young Democrats, Equality California, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund, plus several informal voting-guide groups.

In her own Ballotpedia survey she says she is endorsed by Reps. Robert Garcia, Derek Tran and Dave Min; Controller Malia Cohen; Sens. Tom Umberg and Bob Archuleta; and several Assemblymembers, including Rick Chavez Zbur, Tina McKinnor, Alex Lee, Avelino Valencia, José Luis Solache Jr. and Christopher Ward. This is a candidate claim.

cands.gaps: Swift has never held office, so there is no record of her actions in government. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion beyond a general 'reproductive freedom' line, or school choice and teacher pay. Her birth city, where she grew up, and when she moved to or settled in her current community are not stated. Details of her consulting work and her adjunct teaching post (including the college) were not found. Her campaign priorities pages give only short headings without policy detail.
